question: Does specimen-based taxonomic literature establish a historical Sardinella pacifica association with shared Manila Bay, and can that crosswalk be applied to the 2014 pooled NFRDI ring-net label Sardinella fimbriata?

sources.title: A new species of sardine, Sardinella pacifica from the Philippines (Teleostei, Clupeiformes, Clupeidae)
sources.citation: Hata, H., & Motomura, H. (2019). A new species of sardine, Sardinella pacifica from the Philippines (Teleostei, Clupeiformes, Clupeidae). ZooKeys, 829, 75-83. https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.829.30688.

Materials and examined type-series localities, as reflected in publisher text and the 2025 annotated checklist
sources.accessStatus: PubMed abstract and publisher-indexed full-text output were reviewed. Direct publisher-page retrieval returned 403 and PMC served a reCAPTCHA page; no article file was downloaded or retained. The indexed publisher text exposed the specimen locality and diagnosis used here.
sources.sourceReportedFinding: The description is based on 21 Philippine specimens and names the holotype locality as Manila Harbor, Manila Bay, Luzon. It distinguishes Sardinella pacifica from S. fimbriata using morphology; the 2025 checklist later reports that most type specimens had previously been identified as S. fimbriata.

assessment.historicalLocality: Manila Harbor, Manila Bay, Luzon, Philippines
assessment.evidenceType: Published taxonomic description of preserved type material; not an ecological survey or recent field observation.
assessment.taxonomicFinding: Sardinella pacifica is described as a distinct species from S. fimbriata; the current Catalog of Fishes treats S. pacifica as valid. The 2025 checklist reports that most type specimens had previously carried the S. fimbriata identification.
assessment.typeSeriesScope: The 2019 description is based on 21 Philippine specimens. The 2025 checklist locates the holotype and several paratype lots in Manila Bay; it also lists type material from other Philippine localities. The Manila Bay association applies only to the named historical lots, not to all 21 specimens or the full bay.
assessment.temporalAndSpatialLimits: The original description did not state collection dates. No specimen coordinate is supplied in the reviewed locality text. Retain only the named Manila Harbor / Manila Bay locality and do not manufacture a point, survey date, modern range boundary, or Cavite municipal-water assignment.
assessment.relationshipToNfrdi2014: The 2014 NFRDI ring-net paper reports pooled length-frequency data under the verbatim label Sardinella fimbriata across nine landing sites and supplies no specimen voucher or taxon-by-site/capture-ground crosswalk. The later type-series taxonomic correction makes the old label a meaningful re-identification lead, but it does not identify those 2014 pooled fish as S. pacifica. Preserve the historical source label unless the actual sample/voucher crosswalk is obtained.
assessment.sharedWaterbodyBoundary: Manila Bay is a shared waterbody. Manila Harbor is not assigned to Cavite, and this review adds no Cavite-only or province-specific capture assignment.

decision.reason: The type locality and Manila Bay paratypes provide a historical, specimen-based named-bay taxon lead. They are not recent occurrence records, and the 2014 pooled NFRDI fishery label has no voucher-level crosswalk. Keep both evidence lanes separate and research-only.

limitations: No collection date or specimen coordinates were stated for the described type material in the reviewed sources.
Type-locality and type-series evidence does not establish current presence, abundance, fishery catchability, diet, safety, legality, or a complete Manila Bay inventory.
Manila Bay is shared; the Manila Harbor type locality is not assigned to Cavite or a municipal-water polygon.
The historical 2014 NFRDI Sardinella fimbriata sample is pooled across nine landing sites and is not crosswalked to a museum voucher; do not automatically rename it Sardinella pacifica.

The 2019 primary article page was not directly retrievable in the browser-reader environment; its PubMed abstract and indexed publisher full-text output were reviewed, with the 2025 ZooKeys checklist providing an independently readable type-series summary.
nextAction: Seek specimen or voucher crosswalks for the 2014 NFRDI pooled ring-net material before any taxonomic relabeling. Continue reviewing separately sourced CALABARZON freshwater, brackish and coastal-water fish evidence; no public species row follows from this historical type-series review alone.
